newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold up on Tokyo, physical buying.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold up on Tokyo, physical buying.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended up from New York's previous close on Japanese and physical buying after a day of noticeably quiet trade and low volumes, bullion dealers said on Monday.
Bullion ended at US$353.00/50 an ounce on Monday against New York's US$352.30/80 close on Friday.
"There was light Japanese buying," one dealer at an international bank said.
Physical buying continued, although Hong Kong still suffered from a tightness in kilobars, dealers said.
One trader reported sales of silver in conjunction with gold buying, in a reversal of last week's situation where players were selling gold and buying silver.
Dealers saw gold prices recovering from its battering and reported market players re-establishing long positions.
"Gold could test higher," said one bullion source.
The range over the next week could be as wide as $351 to $355 per ounce, one trader said, noting his forecast was broad as volatility lingered in gold prices.
Others said the price would shuttle between $352 and $354. Local gold ended HK$3 higher at HK$3,261 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -6.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
